reasons: Lake identity record verifies case name Lo-Ji Sales, Inc. v. New York, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1979-06-11.
Lake citations verify official citation 442 U.S. 319, parallel cites 99 S. Ct. 2319; 60 L. Ed. 2d 920; 5 Media L. Rep. (BNA) 1177, and vendor neutral cite 1979 U.S. LEXIS 107.

defect.evidence_quote: He allowed himself to become a member, if not the leader, of the search party which was essentially a police operation. Once in the store, he conducted a generalized search under authority of an invalid warrant; he was not acting as a judicial officer but as an adjunct law enforcement officer.
defect.problem: The holding is substantively supported but the page holding field is truncated with a terminal ellipsis after 'conducting…'.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the truncated holding with a complete sentence: A magistrate abandons the neutral-and-detached role when he joins and leads execution of an open-ended warrant, conducts a generalized search, and directs seizures; that search violates the Fourth Amendment.

reasons: The opinion directly supports the neutral-and-detached magistrate proposition.

The opinion also supports the open-ended/general-warrant component: the warrant left it to search officials to decide what items were obscene, and the Court said the Fourth Amendment does not permit such action.
residual_risks: The disclosed lake record has pinpoints but no separate canonical holding field, so support rests on the full opinion text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use the complete proposed holding rather than a truncated sentence.

reasons: The Neutral and Detached Magistrate home role is supported because the opinion centers on the Town Justice's loss of neutrality and detachment.
The opinion states that the Town Justice did not manifest the neutrality and detachment demanded of a judicial officer and became a member, if not leader, of the search party.
residual_risks: No separate home-page taxonomy file was disclosed, but the case text supports this role at the stated breadth.

defect.locator_note: frontmatter homes entry for The Good-Faith Exception
defect.problem: The Good-Faith Exception home role is not verifiable from the disclosed Lo-Ji evidence. Lo-Ji predates Leon and does not itself analyze the good-faith exception; the lake record shows Leon only as a citing/mentioned progeny edge without a disclosed Leon quote or holding tying Lo-Ji to good faith.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove this home role or replace it with Exclusionary Rule unless a disclosed Leon authority record/pinpoint is added showing that Lo-Ji supplies the abandoned-magistrate boundary of the good-faith exception.

reasons: The Lo-Ji opinion supports suppression for an invalid open-ended warrant and a magistrate's participation in execution, but it contains no good-faith-exception discussion.
The disclosed lake record's Leon edge is only a progeny/treatment edge with field_iii 'mentioned', not evidence of the asserted good-faith role.
The page's own Appears on section lists The Exclusionary Rule rather than The Good-Faith Exception, increasing the placement uncertainty.
residual_risks: This may be legally true if Leon materials are supplied, but it is not proven from this review bundle.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Disclose and cite the Leon pinpoint if retaining this as a Good-Faith Exception cross-doctrine case.
